findings.quote: For a parabola (the curve of $y=ax^2+bx+c$ with $a\ne0$), also check the **turning point**.
findings.problem: The range teaching covers a parabola only on a domain with two ends. The lesson sets the default domain as all real numbers, yet it never teaches the range of a parabola on a domain with no end on a side (for example $y=x^2-4x+5$ on all real numbers gives $[1,\infty)$). It never says that the sign of $a$ decides whether the turning point gives the least or the greatest output, and it does not point to the types-of-functions lesson that teaches opening direction. The shortcut 'test the two end values' has no end values to test in this case. Example 3 states 'There $h(2)=1$, the smallest output' with no reason. The range of a quadratic on its natural domain is a standard application of the range skill in this lesson's goal.
findings.source: content-checklist L18 and L27; brief item 'Find range from a rule and stated input domain' (ustet-L091, dcat-L056, official curriculum); writer-rules lead ruling 1

findings.problem: Example 7 factors $x^2-4$ as a difference of two squares and then solves a quadratic inequality. The lesson does not teach this factoring and does not name the lesson that does (the polynomials lesson teaches the difference of two squares; the quadratic-equations lesson teaches quadratic inequalities). The reader rules require every formula or method an example uses to be taught or its prerequisite named. A one-line pointer would close it.
findings.source: reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit; content-checklist L25; lesson-style-guide, Teaching completeness (reuse rule)
